I'll inspect the weights by hand for anything that doesn't look like a trained tic-tac-toe parameter.

The hidden neuron at index 32 (the last row of W1) is the anomaly. Every one of its 27 input weights is negative, and its bias is negative too. Since every input is 0 or 1, this neuron's pre-activation can never be positive, so ReLU always outputs 0. It is a dead neuron that never affects play, which makes it a perfect place to stash data without changing the network's behavior.

Its outgoing weights in W2 (the last entry of each of the 9 output rows) are:

| Output row | Weight |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0.82 |
| 1 | 0.73 |
| 2 | 0.83 |
| 3 | 0.65 |
| 4 to 8 | 0.0 |

Exactly four nonzero values, each a clean two-decimal number, followed by exact zeros. Scaled by 100 they become 82, 73, 83, 65, which are the ASCII codes for R, I, S, A.

CODE: RISA
